meta._doc: The story_brief is the bridge artifact produced by the ideation front-stage (a sparring-partner dialogue) and consumed by find-data + the orchestrator's Stage-0 input dispatch. It converts a vague reader idea into a concrete, data-backed topic plus a structured data-needs spec. NOT a newsroom pipeline role: it runs upstream of Detective, before any dataset exists, and emits no provenance ids that reach the HTML. Written to <DATA_DIR>/meta/story_brief.json AFTER find-data's audit (so it stays outside the data-file glob). Real data only: this artifact is never a justification to synthesize data — if no real dataset supports the brief, ideation aborts honestly. The example below is illustrative; replace every value.

story_brief.topic: How England's councils diverged on household recycling, 2010-2023
story_brief.angle: Neighbouring authorities with similar budgets ended up 30 points apart - the gap is about policy, not wealth.
story_brief.audience: General readers who follow local-government / environment stories; numerate but not specialist.
questions: Which councils improved most, and which went backwards, over the period?
Does the recycling rate track region, urban/rural, or collection scheme more than income?

data_needs.min_scale: ~300+ council-year rows so contrasts are robust (find-data Gate 2 wants >= ~50 rows)

candidate_sources: DEFRA 'Local authority collected waste management' statistics on gov.uk - a REAL lead surfaced in dialogue, to be verified by find-data, not asserted as fact here.

find_data_invocation.query: England local authority household recycling rate by council 2010 to 2023

story_brief.acceptance: A returned dataset matches IFF it has council-level rows, an annual recycling-rate metric, and >= ~5 years of coverage. If it is national-only, or a single year, or has no rate column, checkpoint-2 sends it back.
open_questions: Is council-level granularity published every year, or are there gaps / boundary changes to reconcile?

_field_notes.topic: one line, headline-ish subject the reader wants to tell.
_field_notes.angle: the tension / argument / surprise - the 'so what' that makes it a story, not just a table.
_field_notes.audience: who it is for; sets tone and the granularity the data must reach.
_field_notes.questions: 1-3 concrete questions the DATA must be able to answer. These are the feasibility anchors for the pressure-test.
_field_notes.data_needs.entities: the unit(s) of observation: cities? countries? players? species? companies?
_field_notes.data_needs.metrics: the numeric variable(s) the story hinges on (>= 1). Without one, the Analyst has nothing to compute.
_field_notes.data_needs.breakdowns: dimension(s) of variation the contrast needs: time / geography / category.
_field_notes.data_needs.time_range: desired temporal coverage AND granularity (annual? monthly? one snapshot?).
_field_notes.data_needs.geography: spatial scope, if any (a country, a region, global).
_field_notes.data_needs.min_scale: rough row count / size needed for the claim to hold; ties to find-data Gate 2.
_field_notes.data_needs.subject_class: concrete | abstract. concrete = people/places/species/events/objects (real photos exist -> richer multimedia, find-data Gate 4); abstract = rates/indices/derived metrics (chart-led, exempted).
_field_notes.candidate_sources: ONLY real leads surfaced during the dialogue (a named gov portal, OWID, a known dataset). NEVER fabricate a source or URL. find-data verifies these; the brief only proposes.
_field_notes.find_data_invocation.query: the exact free-text string passed to /find-data (drives its web search).
_field_notes.find_data_invocation.mode: single (one source -> one folder) | theme (multi-source assembly).
_field_notes.find_data_invocation.flags: optional find-data flags, e.g. --out (recommended, set by ideation), --source.
_field_notes.acceptance: the checkpoint-2 test: the minimum a returned dataset MUST contain to count as matching this brief.
_field_notes.open_questions: unresolved bits the data search itself might settle (gaps, definitions, boundary changes).
